“A valuable grilled fish restaurant in front of Ewha Womans University”

There is a fairly famous grilled fish restaurant in front of Yeondae in Sinchon, but it is unfortunate that there is no grilled fish restaurant in the area in front of Ewha Womans University, which is slightly up the road.
A new restaurant recently opened near Sinchon Train Station, and to my delight, it specializes in grilled fish.
It's a distance worth going even if you have to work a little harder.

The menu includes not only grilled fish, but also stir-fried dishes such as stir-fried pork, bulgogi, and squid bulgogi, as well as cheonggukjang, pollack hangover soup, whole pollack stew, and egg stew, making it a menu where you can eat and drink.

All of the side dishes were delicious and there were many flavor variations.

Well-cooked grilled mackerel cannot be without its taste. This place has pretty good grilling skills.
It is a great meal with side dishes.

It has a fairly deep and refreshing taste, moistening meals that would otherwise be dry.

lol? Carrying it with effort. The first thing he said was, "It's the person who bought it earlier. It's wasabi tuna mayo, but it doesn't taste like wasabi." Just say this.

"There's no way there's no wasabi...?"

They say it tastes different from yesterday and that the amount of wasabi may vary because it is wrapped by hand.
?????
And if you want a lot of wasabi, ask for more wasabi next time??
No, the amount I already packed is already different. What are you talking about???

#Sinchon #Neunggok grandmother pollack soup

“High-end ramen?”

This is a place I wanted to visit after seeing it as a foodie.
The head office is in Neunggok and the house where he appeared on TV is in Ilsan, and it is said that Ilsan is the son of the grandmother of the head office.
But the taste is a little different haha.
This restaurant is a franchise branch of the main branch, and since they opened one in Sinchon, I was curious and tried it.

When I ordered for one person, I was given a mulgun soup with a whole dried pollack.
I boiled it as directed and tried the soup, and it was very refreshing.
The soup is very helpful for the drinker, and this kind of soup seems to be perfect for hangovers when eating out.

Instead, kimchi does the hard work.
Instead of cutting large cabbage leaves as instructed, you must tear them with your hands and eat them.
Although it may be a bit inconvenient, it is delicious when served with rice in a retro way.
Quite refreshing commercial cabbage kimchi!

The rice is also good because it is served straight from the bowl rather than air-cooked rice.

The long-awaited ramen time.
Adding ramen completely changes the taste.
It's refreshing, but the ramen flavor comes out great.
It tastes like eating premium pollack ramen, and once Masada tastes this, he won't be able to stop eating it!

Egg rolls are made with only salt and no MSG, making them a great mouth-watering treat.

I like this place.
I hope you stay for a long time and help me with my glass of soju and my hangover haha.

reviews.text:
This is a vegan restaurant with the concept of ‘temple food in the city’ located in the food court (2nd floor) near Sinchon Station. It's great for dining alone, and because there are a variety of restaurants, it's also convenient for dining with friends who aren't vegetarian or vegan.

Drinks are self-service. The free peach earl gray tea is really delicious. So far, I've tried pork cutlet, snowflake salad, avocado roll, and cream curry udon. At first, I was a little hesitant about the pork cutlet because the texture and taste were different from what I expected, but after that, I kept thinking about it and came back several times. It comes with a small salad, rice, and sauce, making it a complete meal.
The snowflake salad is also delicious, and it's great to eat in times like these when it's hard to find fresh vegetables in Seoul. However, olives were not my taste. The avocado roll was bigger than expected and tasted pretty good. I think it will taste better if you dip it in soy sauce. Cream curry udon is perfect when you want something hearty and warm, but I personally don't think I'll order it again.

The owner seemed very kind. One time I couldn't finish the avocado roll, and they packaged the rest for me. I think payment is only possible by card. I recommend it if you're nearby and looking for a quick place to have lunch.

After taking classes at J Life School in Sinchon on Tuesdays and Thursdays of every month and exploring the restaurants in Sinchon and Ewha Womans University, the first restaurant we visited was Gonaengji.

This restaurant is recommended by everyone who takes classes with me. It is located about halfway between Sinchon and Ewha Womans University and is located just across the street from Sinchon train station.

For two people, I recommend kimchi stew and egg rolls.

Egg rolls are egg rolls the size of served as a side dish to alcohol.
The amount of kimchi stew is such that it would be burdensome to eat alone.
Half a ramen sari is included as standard, so there is no need to add a separate ramen.

What's unusual is that in a typical restaurant, the menu is determined based on the contents inside.
For high cold regions, you can choose basic kimchi stew with toppings such as pork or tuna.

As for the interior, it has a sophisticated interior, perhaps because it is geographically a place with a lot of students, so I think it would be a suitable place for a date.

To evaluate the taste, it's actually a very delicious restaurant!!!! It is difficult to say this, but

This restaurant definitely exists for a reason that many people recommend it!!!

The peanut caramel served for dessert is a restaurant filled with emotions that stimulate memories!!!

#Sinchon #Changcheon-dong #Gobau

“My favorite salt grill restaurant”

I already wrote about this restaurant in my first review, but this restaurant is a memorable one for me.
I found this place after reminiscing about happy memories from 25 years ago, and it is now my favorite salt grill restaurant.

The number of customers has increased significantly compared to when I first discovered it.
The grandmother owner has now retired from the front line and is taking a break, while her son, his wife, and granddaughter are working hard to run the store.

The food at this restaurant is delicious, but the price is still the same.
In the past, the price was a whopping 10,000 won for 200g, but now with skyrocketing prices, the price is 11,000 won for 180g.
Although it has gone up a bit, the price is still very competitive.

The beef hangover soup provided as standard is delicious, and the kimchi provided upon request is a match made in heaven with pork, isn't it?

I hope that you will always remain the best salt grill in Sinchon.

Donbul 1971, located in Sinchon, is a meat restaurant that impresses with its method of grilling raw Jeju meat over charcoal briquettes. The deep fire aroma from the meat was excellent, and both the Jeju pork belly and pork neck were juicy and clean without any unpleasant smell.
What I especially liked was the service where the staff first cuts the meat, prepares it, and then grills it directly at the table. Thanks to this, even beginners can enjoy meat comfortably, and the taste remains consistent.
The side dishes are also plentiful and thoughtful. It consists of green onion green onion, white kimchi, wasabi, and fermented soybean paste that go well with meat, and I was also satisfied with the Yangpoon bibimbap and steamed egg that I ordered as a side. The steamed egg custard had a strong umami flavor, perhaps because it used katsuobushi broth.

The atmosphere of the store has a retro, old-fashioned feel. Thanks to the drum tables and a slightly noisy atmosphere, it seemed like it would be a good place for a company dinner or gathering.
The price is also relatively reasonable. Jeju Ogyeopsal is priced around 12,000 Won per serving, and Gochujang Bulgogi is priced around 10,000 Won, so I felt it was good value for money.
Here's a tip: If you order red pepper paste bulgogi first, raw meat orders may be limited due to problems with grill replacement, so I recommend that you choose your order carefully.

This is a restaurant I want to visit again!
